title: Diabetes, hypertension and CKD together
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's diabetes, kidney disease and any related hypertension and dialysis status.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for chronic kidney disease and hypertension.

HPI
The patient is a 68-year-old male presenting for a scheduled follow-up of his chronic kidney disease and hypertension. He reports feeling generally well today with no new concerns regarding his symptoms. He currently manages his type 2 diabetes through diet and exercise alone. He denies any recent changes in his renal function or significant fluctuations in his blood pressure at home.

Medication List
Lisinopril 10 mg daily
Amlodipine 5 mg daily

Exam
The patient appears in no acute distress. He is alert and oriented. Blood pressure is 138/82 mmHg. Heart rate is 72 beats per minute. Lungs are clear to auscultation. No pedal edema is noted.

Assessment
1. Chronic kidney disease, stage 4. Recent labs show an eGFR of 22.
2. Hypertension.
3. Type 2 diabetes.

Plan
Continue current medications for hypertension and CKD. Patient will continue to manage his type 2 diabetes with dietary modifications. We will monitor renal function and blood pressure at the next visit in three months.

Electronically signed, K. Nguyen, PA-C
October 14, 2026
explanations: Type 2 diabetes and CKD are linked by the 'with' convention unless the provider says otherwise: E11.22 (HCC 37).
Hypertension with CKD stage 1-4 is presumed linked: I12.9. Both links apply at once: diabetes with CKD and hypertensive CKD.
The CKD stage is coded in addition: N18.4.

distractors.why: The 'with' convention presumes the diabetes caused the CKD.
Hypertension and CKD are presumed linked: I12.-, not I10.
I12.0 is for stage 5 or ESRD only.
E11.22 says to use an additional code for the CKD stage.
